title: The "waiting on something" notice that won't go away

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: What is going on today

calls.why: You press send while Claude Code is waiting for you to answer a question or permission card, or a pop-up in its terminal. Your message is NOT sent; it stays in the box.

calls.call: Why does it never go away?
calls.why: It is meant to vanish after 8 seconds, but a mistake restarts that countdown every time the screen updates. While Claude works, that is many times a second.

calls.call: Why does it follow you to other chats?
calls.why: The app has a single spot for floating notices, shared by the whole window. It does not belong to any one chat, so switching chats leaves it showing.

calls.call: Other floating notices have the same bug
calls.why: About 40 other short notices use that same spot, like "Not connected" or "Couldn't switch model". All of them can get stuck the same way while Claude works.

calls.call: Most other chat warnings already behave the way you want
calls.why: "Claude seems stuck", sign-in problems, "this message didn't send", the "Connecting…" band and "Claude Code is asking something" each belong to one chat and vanish once the problem is fixed.

steps.intro: Four decisions. The first one matters most; the rest follow from it.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: Where should this notice live, and when should it go away?
steps.today: It floats over the bottom of the chat, is shared by every chat, and is meant to vanish after 8 seconds but gets stuck instead.
steps.checked: Read in the app's current code on 2026-11-21, and matches your screenshot.
steps.problem: It covers your messages, follows you to chats it has nothing to do with, and can stay long after you answered the card.
steps.proposal: Three ways to fix it. All three stop it following you to other chats.

options.label: A strip above the box
options.summary: A one-line strip directly above the message box, in that chat only, like the existing "Connecting…" strip. It stays until you answer the card, close the pop-up, or send a message.
pros: Works like the app's other per-chat warnings, so nothing new to learn.
Another notice can't push it away while the problem is still there.
cons: Takes one line of space above the box while it shows.
A bit more work than the other two.

options.label: Floating, per chat
options.summary: Stays a floating bubble like today, but only on its own chat, and stays until you answer, close the pop-up, or send.
pros: Looks the same as today; only when it leaves changes.
cons: A bubble that stays can still cover messages, which is what bothers you now.
Any other notice that pops up would replace it.

options.label: Just fix the timer
options.summary: Keep it as it is, but make it really leave after 8 seconds, and when you switch chats.
cons: It can disappear while the card is still unanswered, leaving you unsure why your message didn't go.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: Should the notice appear only after you try to send?
steps.today: It appears only when you press send and the message is held back.
steps.checked: Read in the app's current code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: If it showed every time Claude Code waits on you, it would repeat a card that is usually already in plain view.
steps.proposal: Keep it as now: it appears only after a send is held back. Yes keeps that; No makes it show whenever something is waiting, even before you type.

steps.headline: Once you answer the card, should your held-back message send itself?
steps.today: Your message stays in the box. After answering the card you press send again yourself.
steps.checked: Read in the app's current code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: Pressing send twice is a small annoyance, but a message sending itself later can surprise you.

options.label: You press send again
options.summary: The message waits in the box until you send it, as it does now.
pros: Nothing sends without you pressing the button.
You can change or delete the message first.

options.label: It sends itself
options.summary: The strip says "Your message will send once you answer", and it goes out as soon as you do.
cons: A message typed minutes ago could go out after you forgot it or changed your mind.
A bigger change to how sending works, so more that could go wrong.

steps.path: The notices above the message box
steps.headline: Should I also fix the stuck timer for the other floating notices now?
steps.today: About 40 short notices, like "Not connected" or "Couldn't switch model", share the same timer mistake and can stay on screen while Claude works.
steps.checked: Found by reading the shared notice code on 2026-11-21; the mistake is in one place all of them use.
steps.problem: Any of them can get stuck on screen the same way this one did.
steps.proposal: Fix that one shared mistake now, separately from this notice. Yes fixes it; the only thing you would notice is those notices leaving on time. No leaves them as they are.
